statement.p: Use Lagrange multipliers to find the maximum and minimum values of f(x,y) = 4 x - 3 y subject to the constraint x^2 + 3 y^2 = 171, if such values exist.

p.em: (For either value, enter DNE if there is no such value.)

static.solution: f(x,y)= 4 x - 3 y and our equation of constraint is g(x,y) = x^2 + 3 y^2 = 171. To optimize f(x,y) with Lagrange multipliers we solve the following system of equations f_{x}(x,y) = \lambda g_{x}(x,y),\qquad\mbox{so } 4 = 2\lambda x, f_{y}(x,y) = \lambda g_{y}(x,y),\qquad\mbox{so } -3 = 6\lambda y, and g(x,y) = 171,\qquad\mbox{so } x^2 + 3 y^2 = 171. Solving for \lambda gives us \lambda = \frac{2}{ x} = \frac{-1}{2 y}, which we can use to find x in terms of y: x = -4\,y. Using this relation in our equation of constraint, we can solve for y: x^2 + 3 y^2 = 171, so (-4\, y)^2 + 3 y^2 = 171, and thus ((4)^2 + 3)\, y^2 = 171. So, solving for y, we have y = \pm 3, and x = \mp 12. Thus, the critical points are (-12,3) and (12,-3). Since the constraint is closed and bounded, maximum and minimum values of f subject to the constraint exist. Evaluating f at the critical points, we find that the maximum value is f(12,-3) = 4(12) + 3(3) = 57 and the minimum value is f(-12,3) = -4(12) - 3(3) = -57.
